feat(feishu): preserve image/text ordering in post messages

Feishu post (rich text) messages can interleave text and images, but the
old code extracted text and images in two separate passes and dropped all
positional information. The model received "textA\ntextB\ntextC" with
[img1, img2] as attachments and could not tell which image went with
which paragraph.

Merge the two helpers into extractPostInterleaved() which walks the post
once and inlines [图N] placeholders (1-indexed) into the text wherever an
img tag appeared. The returned imageKeys array is ordered to match, so
callers can keep using imageKeys[0] as the primary image and slice(1) as
extraMedia without changing the downstream contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(bridge): label downloaded image paths to match [Image N] anchors

The prior commit injected [Image N] placeholders into post text, but
message-bridge still emitted "[Image saved at: <imageKey>.png]" — the
agent had no way to tell which placeholder pointed at which file.

- Renumber the text placeholders as [Image N] (1-indexed)
- Label the main download as "[Image 1 saved at: ...]"
- Walk extraMedia with an imageCounter so files come out as
  [Image 2 saved at: ...], [Image 3 saved at: ...], etc; non-image
  attachments don't bump the counter

test(feishu): lock post image/text ordering through the dispatcher

Covers the three review asks on #320: direct and locale-wrapped post
shapes, interleaved text/images, and post images combined with cached
group media. Tests drive createEventDispatcher end-to-end (schema 2.0
events, needCheck: false) and assert the [Image N] anchor invariant:
the first image rides as imageKey, the rest follow as extraMedia in
placeholder order, and cached media appends after post extras without
ever claiming an anchor.

Also fixes a stale [图N] reference in the extractPostInterleaved
docstring left over from the [Image N] rename.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(build): make pack-metabot.sh work with BSD tar on macOS (#362)

`npm run build` failed on macOS at the pack:metabot step with
`tar: Option --sort=name is not supported`: the deterministic-archive
flags (--sort=name, --owner/--group, --mtime) are GNU tar extensions,
and macOS ships BSD tar (bsdtar), which rejects them.

Detect a GNU tar first (`tar`, then Homebrew's `gtar`) and keep the
exact original invocation when one is found, so Linux CI behavior is
unchanged. Otherwise fall back to a BSD-compatible pipeline that
preserves the same determinism guarantees:

1. Stage the payload through bsdtar itself so the TAR_EXCLUDES
   patterns keep their create-time recursion semantics.
2. Pin every staged mtime to 2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC (the same
   instant GNU's --mtime pins).
3. Archive an explicitly pre-sorted member list (find | LC_ALL=C sort,
   recursion off) with uid/gid forced to 0, in gnutar format, piped
   through `gzip -n` for a timestamp-free header.

Verified on macOS 26.5 (bsdtar 3.5.3): two consecutive packs produce
byte-identical tarballs, the personal flavor passes its static-leak
self-check, the pack-metabot vitest smoke suite passes (15/15), and
the full `npm run build` succeeds.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(bridge): stop replaying delivered output files on follow-up turns (#352)

* fix(bridge): stop replaying delivered output files on follow-up turns

prepareDir keeps files younger than the 5-minute retention window and
scanOutputs is a stateless directory walk, so every follow-up message
inside that window resent the entire outputs directory ("thanks" →
here is report.pdf again).

Bind delivery to deletion: files that were sent, text-fallbacked, or
accounted for via the oversized notice are unlinked after handling;
files whose send threw stay on disk so the next turn retries them.

The two resend tests fail on the unfixed code (bug reproduction); the
retry test locks the keep-on-throw semantics.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(bridge): mark output files delivered only on confirmed delivery

Review follow-up: sendImageFile/sendLocalFile resolve false on
non-throwing send failures, but delivery-bound deletion treated every
non-throwing path as delivered and unlinked files the user never
received.

- image sends: delivered = the actual boolean send result
- file sends: delivered on true, or on a successful text fallback;
  a false return with no applicable fallback retains the file
- oversized files: deletion deferred until the coalesced notice
  actually reached the user; a failed notice retains them so the
  next turn re-raises it
- tests: image false-return, file false-return without fallback,
  text-fallback delivery, notice failure + re-raise

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(pty): match Claude projects-dir escaping

Claude Code escapes the cwd to ~/.claude/projects/<escaped> by replacing
EVERY non-alphanumeric character with '-' (not just '/'). Verified against
live dirs: /u/openclaw_workspace → -u-openclaw-workspace, ~/.openclaw →
--openclaw.

metabot replaced only '/', so for any cwd containing '_' (or '.', spaces…)
the pty jsonl scanner tailed a nonexistent path, no assistant records ever
reached the stream processor, and every reply came back empty while the
turn itself completed normally (thinking → done, no message).

- session-lister claudeProjectsDir(): escape [^a-zA-Z0-9-] → '-'
- pty-session: derive jsonlPath via shared claudeProjectsDir() (single
  source of truth, as the session-lister comment already demands)
- tests: cover underscore + dotted-directory escaping

Closes #373

Co-authored-by: lvjunliang <lvjunliang@users.noreply.gitee.com>
